Here in the US, gun dealers are under strong pressure to go above and beyond common sense measures.

Every sale requires a federal background check, which literally means calling the feds up on the phone and getting an explicit OK. It requires the user to fill out and sign a long form, explicitly disclaiming any of a number of reasons why they might not be eligible to purchase a gun. The seller is responsible for checking every detail on that form, and is also responsible for denying the sale if they have any reason to believe the purchaser is buying a gun for someone else. They get audited frequently and their license to do business will be quickly pulled if they screw this up.

And that's just the regulatory side. On the civil side, if they sell a gun to a prohibited person who then goes on to commit a crime, they can be sued for massive damages, and they have very little wiggle room to cover their mistakes. Every step in the process is explicitly documented.

Compare this to bar tenders, who routinely sell alcohol to people who are expected to then drive themselves home. Nothing is documented, and anything but the most egregious misconduct is impossible to prove.
